system.name: Cilantro
system.one_liner: a framework that allocates a single fungible resource among competing jobs by continuously learning each job's resource-to-performance mapping from live feedback

components.name: Shared Cluster
components.role: holds the competing jobs that resources are allocated among

components.name: Job 1
components.role: one job running in the shared cluster

components.name: Job 2
components.role: another job running in the shared cluster, competing for the same resource

components.name: Per-Job Feedback
components.role: continuous live feedback from each job (e.g., its P95 SLO versus actual P95) used to learn performance mappings

components.name: Cilantro Scheduler
components.role: groups the online learners and policy that together compute resource allocations

components.name: Online Learners
components.role: a pool of performance learners and load forecasters that estimate each job's resource-performance curve from live feedback

components.name: Policy
components.role: scheduling policy, automatically derived from the user's objective, that uses the learned models to compute allocations

components.name: User-defined Objective
components.role: the end user's declared scheduling objective that instantiates the policy

components.name: Resource Allocations
components.role: the computed per-job allocation amounts (e.g., Job 1: 40, Job 2: 60) applied to the cluster

content.key_idea: Cilantro closes a feedback loop around a shared cluster: it continuously learns each job's resource-to-performance mapping from live per-job feedback, then uses a policy derived from the user's declared objective to turn those learned models into resource allocations, becoming more accurate and effective over time.
content.reading_order: Left to right and back: jobs in the Shared Cluster emit per-job feedback that flows up into the Online Learners, whose performance models feed the Policy (instantiated for the user-defined objective), which sends resource allocations back down to the cluster.

summary: Figure 2 gives Cilantro's high-level architecture as a closed feedback loop. Jobs (Job 1, Job 2, ...) run in a Shared Cluster and emit Per-Job Feedback, illustrated with an example where a job's actual P95 latency (125ms) exceeds its 100ms SLO. This feedback continuously trains a pool of Online Learners, which maintain a Performance Model per job estimating its resource-to-performance curve. The Cilantro Scheduler's Policy, automatically instantiated for the end user's declared objective, consumes these learned models to compute Resource Allocations (e.g., Job 1: 40, Job 2: 60) that are applied back to the cluster. Because the loop runs continuously, Cilantro's allocations improve as its learned models become more accurate, without requiring an offline performance model ahead of time.
summary_zh: 图2展示Cilantro架构：共享集群中各作业产生反馈（如P95实际值超SLO），训练在线学习器得到资源-性能模型；调度器据用户目标计算资源分配（如Job1:40）并作用回集群，形成闭环，分配随之变优。
notes: layout-proposal: closed-loop scheduler — a Shared Cluster and a Cilantro Scheduler box connected by a feedback arrow (up) and an allocation arrow (down) forming a closed control loop; 'hub-spoke' is used as the closest named template with the scheduler as hub over per-job spokes, though the loop shape is not a classic radial hub-spoke.
